findings.issue_text: [BUG] The diff adds a `sentry-repo` gitlink (submodule) pointing at commit a5d290951de, which is not a real submodule of this repository and has no .gitmodules entry. Anyone cloning with --recurse-submodules or CI checking out the PR gets a broken/missing submodule checkout; the repo tree is corrupted by an accidental nested-repo artifact.

[BUG] The `upsampled_count` implementation references a `sample_weight` column (`Function("sum", [Column("sample_weight")])`) that has no writer anywhere in this diff — `store_event`'s new hook only sets a `sample_rate` key on normalized_data, and no code, processor, or snuba schema change maps it into a `sample_weight` column. Every upsampled query sent to Snuba fails with an unknown-column error (or silently sums to 0), returning 500s/bogus zeros to allowlisted orgs instead of counts; the API test asserting count==10 cannot pass because sample_weight is never populated.

[BUG] `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` compares the passed `dataset` object against the `sentry.snuba.errors` / `transactions` / `discover` modules, but `organization_events_stats` passes the value from `get_dataset(...)`, which in current sentry is a Dataset class instance (e.g. `DiscoverDataset`), not a module, so all three equality checks are always False. The transform never applies on any dataset, the feature is a silent no-op, and `test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects` (which asserts count==10) fails.

[BUG] `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` writes `normalized_data["sample_rate"]` from a client-supplied context, but no code in this diff (or any consumer shown) reads a top-level `sample_rate` on normalized event data to produce a `sample_weight` column in Snuba. The factory hook is dead-end code: the API tests that rely on it to produce upsampled counts (expected value 10 from client_sample_rate 0.1) get plain count()==1 or 0, so the end-to-end upsampled tests fail.

[BUG] The eligibility cache key is derived only from organization.id and project_ids, but the cached value is consulted for any dataset/query, and `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` compares int project ids against `options.get("issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist", [])` whose real-world option value is a mapping/set of slugs or org-project structures, not a flat list of int ids. Against the actual option store the `project_id in allowlist` check never matches (TypeError on unhashable dict members or plain False), so upsampling silently never activates in production even when configured; the tests only pass because they mock `options.get` to return a list of ints.

[ADVISORY] The 60-second cache stores the allowlist verdict keyed by project-id tuple, so a query across projects A+B poisons a later differently-scoped request only per-tuple, but any allowlist change takes up to 60s to propagate and `invalidate_upsampling_cache` has no caller in this diff (no signal/option-change hook wires it). Operators flipping the allowlist see stale upsampled/plain counts for up to a minute across all stats requests; the invalidation helper is a ships-inert API nobody invokes.

[ADVISORY] The endpoint computes `should_upsample` via a cache-backed helper before every stats query unconditionally, adding a Redis cache round-trip (get, plus set on miss) on a path that previously had no cache call at all. Every organization-events-stats request now pays an extra cache get/set even for orgs with no allowlisted projects, a hot-path regression on one of Sentry's highest-traffic endpoints.

[BUG] The shared 60-second eligibility cache in is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects is never cleared between tests, so test_error_upsampling_with_partial_allowlist reads the True cached by the preceding test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects and fails. test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects caches cache_key 'error_upsampling_eligible:{org}:{hash}' = True via the real Django cache; the very next test patches options to a partial allowlist, but the cache hit short-circuits _are_all_projects_error_upsampled, the query is upsampled, counts come back as 10 instead of 1, and the assertion `assert data[0][1][0]["count"] == 1` fails — the partial-allowlist safety behavior is never actually verified.

[BUG] is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects — the only production entry point, including the cache-hit/cache-miss branches — has zero test coverage; the new test file imports only the private helpers (_are_all_projects_error_upsampled, _is_error_focused_query, _should_apply_sample_weight_transform, transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling) and no test exercises the caching path. The cache-hit branch `return cached_result and _should_apply_sample_weight_transform(dataset, request)` and the cache.set path are untested; a regression in cache key construction or the cached-boolean conjunction ships unnoticed, and the tests-as-written cannot even detect the cache behavior they accidentally depend on (they collide through it, see cache-pollution finding).

[ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache is defined but has no caller anywhere in the diff — it is a ships-inert function, so option changes are only reflected after the hard-coded 60s TTL with no active invalidation path. Operators toggling issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist get up to 60 seconds of stale eligibility (queries silently under- or over-counting sample_weight); the invalidation hook exists but nothing wires it to option-change signals, so the documented consistency mechanism is dead code.

[ADVISORY] Only y_axes/timeseries_columns are transformed for upsampling, but the top-events selection, orderby (self.get_orderby), selected_columns (self.get_field_list), and equations (self.get_equation_list) all keep raw count()/equation semantics — sibling aggregation surfaces on the same rendering path are left untransformed. A topEvents request with orderby=count() and an equation yAxis (e.g. `count()/count_unique(user)`) on allowlisted projects gets top-N series selected and ordered by unweighted count while the returned series values are weighted, and equation components referencing count() inside the equation string are never rewritten (transform only matches the exact column "count()"), producing internally inconsistent widget data for dashboards users.

[ADVISORY] transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling only matches the exact string count(), silently skipping aliased forms ("count() as foo"), count(unique(...)), count_if(...), and any derived column a client sends as yAxis. Users querying yAxis=count() as errors (a documented yAxis form with alias) on allowlisted error-upsampled projects receive unweighted counts with no warning, so the upsampled total silently disagrees with the plain count() widget for the same projects — the acceptance criterion 'error counts are upsampled for allowlisted projects' is only met for the single canonical spelling.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds a stray gitlink/submodule 'sentry-repo' (commit a5d290951de) that is unrelated to the error-upsampling feature and referenced by nothing in the changed code. Every consumer of this repo gains an accidental submodule; CI/checkout behavior changes for all developers and any tooling that enumerates submodules, and the actual sample_weight ingestion work the feature depends on is nowhere verifiable in this PR — the endpoint transformation has no confirmed producer of sample_weight data in the diff besides the test factory hack.

[ADVISORY] _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling is applied unconditionally inside store_event, mutating normalized_data['sample_rate'] for every test event that carries an error_sampling context — a global factory behavior change with no verification that existing store_event consumers are unaffected. Any pre-existing test that stores an event with a contexts.error_sampling block and asserts on sample_rate-derived behavior (retention/interval calculations use sample_rate) now gets different values; the bare `except Exception: pass` around the contexts lookup also silently swallows a non-dict contexts value, hiding shape errors from test authors.

[ADVISORY] upsampled_count is registered only in the discover dataset's function_converter, but _should_apply_sample_weight_transform also returns True for the errors dataset (sentry.snuba.errors), and no test covers an errors-dataset query using the transformed column. If an errors-dataset stats query resolves to a function registry that lacks upsampled_count, the request fails with an unknown-function validation error rather than returning upsampled counts; the errors-dataset path is asserted only indirectly and never exercised with the transformed y_axes.

[BUG] The diff adds a git submodule 'sentry-repo' pointing at commit a5d290951de that has no relationship to the error upsampling feature. Every checkout of this branch gains a nested sentry repo checkout; CI and deployments that don't init submodules silently get an empty tree, and the repo history now carries an unexplained external pointer that no requirement mentions — classic accidental scope pollution that must be removed before merge.

[ADVISORY] The error-message rewording 'If topEvents needs to be at least 1' -> 'topEvents needs to be at least 1' is unrelated to the upsampling feature. Drive-by changes to a public API's error string are not traceable to any requirement in this PR; any client matching on the old message breaks and reviewers of the upsampling change have to audit it anyway.

[ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache() is dead code — no call site exists anywhere in this diff (no options-change hook, admin action, or signal receiver invokes it). Operators who edit 'issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist' have no way to flush the 60s cache via this function, so the shipped 'invalidation' capability is inert; either wire it to the option-update path or delete it, since leaving it implies a consistency guarantee that does not exist.

[ADVISORY] _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling is applied unconditionally inside store_event, mutating global test infrastructure for every test in the codebase, not just upsampling tests. Any existing test whose event data happens to carry contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate now gets a sample_rate injected into normalized data, changing results of unrelated event-processing/tagging tests; the production ingest path has no equivalent logic in this diff, so test factories now diverge from real ingestion behavior.

[ADVISORY] The caching layer is 'performance optimization' work not traceable to the stated requirement, and its cache key omits both the dataset and the query — it caches only project-allowlist eligibility while the returned value is that AND _should_apply_sample_weight_transform(dataset, request). The cache only short-circuits the allowlist check, so a request on the errors dataset and one on the discover dataset with the same projects share one cache entry and re-evaluate the dataset half anyway; meanwhile the 60s staleness window means an operator removing a project from the allowlist keeps serving upsampled counts for up to a minute with no invalidation path — complexity added with no demonstrated requirement behind it.

[ADVISORY] The 'should_upsample'/'upsampling_enabled' boolean pair and the three duplicated 'if upsampling_enabled: final_columns = transform...' blocks are scaffolding that adds no behavior over a single inlined call. final_columns is already initialized to query_columns at line ~226 and transform is idempotent-guarded only by the boolean, so the next editor adding a fourth query branch must remember to replicate the transform block again; deleting the intermediate alias and the per-branch re-application removes three conditional blocks and one variable with zero behavior change.

[BUG] The cache key embeds `hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))`, and Python's built-in hash is salted per process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so different workers compute different keys for the same project set. In production with multiple workers/processes behind the region-silo cache, cache writes from one process are never read by another, so the 60-second cache optimization silently does nothing, and worse, `invalidate_upsampling_cache` (which builds the key in yet another process) deletes a key no serving process will ever look up — cache invalidation is structurally broken, allowing stale allowlist decisions beyond the intended 60s window with no working invalidation path.

[ADVISORY] `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined but no code anywhere in the diff (no signal handler, option-change hook, admin path, or test) calls it. Operators changing `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` have no wired-up invalidation path; the exported function is dead code whose existence implies a consistency guarantee the system does not actually provide — a maintainer relying on it ships stale-eligibility bugs.

[BUG] `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns True for the `errors` dataset, but the `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction is only registered in the discover dataset's `function_converter` (src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py:1041-1052); the errors dataset has no such function. Any query routed through the errors dataset with `count()` in its y-axes gets `upsampled_count()` substituted into a column list the errors dataset resolver cannot translate, producing a query-resolution failure (500 / empty series) for exactly the allowlisted projects this feature is meant to serve.

[ADVISORY] `_is_error_focused_query` is a raw substring check for `"event.type:error"` in the lowercased query string, so discover-dataset queries that target errors without that literal token (e.g. `error.value:foo`, `exception.type:ValueError`, or a default no-filter query on an errors-only project) are not upsampled, while `"event.type:errorhandshake"` would be. Users on allowlisted projects see count() flip between upsampled and raw values depending on whether they happen to include the literal `event.type:error` token — the same underlying events report different counts across saved dashboards/alerts that differ only in query phrasing, undermining trust in the whole feature.

[ADVISORY] `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` only rewrites the exact literal `count()`, leaving `count() as foo`, `count_unique(user)`, `count_if(...)`, and equations untouched. A single multi-axis request (e.g. `yAxis=count(),count_unique(user)`) returns one upsampled series alongside one raw series on the same chart, producing internally inconsistent data for allowlisted projects; the alias form `count() as total` silently stays raw, so callers who alias their counts get non-upsampled numbers with no error.

[ADVISORY] `upsampled_count` declares `default_result_type="number"` while the `count()` function it replaces uses `"integer"`. Downstream consumers that branch on result type (chart formatting, alert threshold comparison, serialization hints) treat the upsampled count as a float/number where the same axis previously reported integer, causing format changes and potential strict-type mismatches in alert conditions for allowlisted projects.

[ADVISORY] `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` mutates `normalized_data` inside the global `store_event` factory, affecting every test in the entire suite that stores an event with an `error_sampling` context, not just the upsampling tests. Any existing or future test fixture that includes an `error_sampling` context now silently gains a `sample_rate` on the normalized event, changing event-processor behavior in unrelated tests and creating cross-suite coupling where a test factory change for one feature alters normalization results everywhere.

[BUG] The 60-second eligibility cache is never invalidated because invalidate_upsampling_cache has zero call sites anywhere in the diff, so allowlist changes silently fail to propagate for up to 60 seconds per cached project-set. An operator removes a project from issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist and the org-events-stats endpoint keeps returning sum(sample_weight)-based (upsampled) counts for that project for 60s — and conversely, a newly allowlisted project keeps getting raw count() — with no code path to force consistency; the docstring's 'eventual consistency is acceptable' rationale was never accepted by anyone since the invalidation hook it implies is dead code.

[ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache is ships-inert dead code: no endpoint, options-change hook, or signal handler in this diff calls it, and it only deletes one exact project-set key, so even a future caller could not clear the unbounded cross-product of project_id tuples already cached. Whoever later assumes cache invalidation exists (the docstring tells them it does) gets silently stale eligibility decisions; the function's existence documents an intent (revoke-on-change) that the diff never actually implements.

[BUG] The feature's stated objective — upsampled error counts — is silently reduced to a no-op against real data: nothing in the diff (or anywhere reachable from it) writes a sample_weight value for error events; the only new writer sets a top-level 'sample_rate' field in the test factory (tests/sentry/testutils/factories.py:344-358), which no production code reads or converts into the sample_weight column that upsampled_count() sums. In production, allowlisted projects' event rows have no populated sample_weight, so toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) returns 0 or null instead of an upsampled count — the headline behavior of the PR is only demonstrated by a test-time factory hack, meaning review iterations replaced 'support upsampling' with 'plumb a transformation that assumes upstream data that doesn't exist yet'.

[ADVISORY] The cache key uses Python's per-process salted hash(): 'error_upsampling_eligible:{org.id}:{hash(tuple(...))}', which is non-deterministic across processes and even across interpreter restarts, so entries stored via a shared cache backend (Redis/memcached) are unreadable by any other worker and keys churn every restart. Every gunicorn/region-silo worker computes a different key for the same project set, so the 'performance optimization' provides near-zero hit rate in the multi-process deployment it was added for, while still paying the cache.set cost on every worker; use a stable digest (e.g. md5 of the sorted ids) instead.

[ADVISORY] Hooking _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling into the global store_event factory silently mutates normalized_data for every event in the entire test suite that happens to carry an error_sampling context, changing sample_rate-driven behavior (retention/sampling assertions) in unrelated tests with no opt-in. Any existing test that stores an event with a contexts.error_sampling blob and asserts on sample_rate-derived behavior now sees a different payload than before this PR; the change is invisible in test failures that will be blamed on the tests rather than this global side effect.

[ADVISORY] The diff smuggles in an unrelated public-API behavior change: the 400 response body for topEvents <= 0 changes from 'If topEvents needs to be at least 1' to 'topEvents needs to be at least 1' with no acceptance trail, breaking any client that string-matches the error detail. Downstream consumers or test fixtures matching the old detail text start failing after deploy; a typo fix belongs in its own change, not embedded in an upsampling PR where it evades review of the contract change.

[BUG] The new upsampled_count() SnQL function is registered in the public function_converter without private=True, exposing it to arbitrary API clients. Any authenticated user of any organization can pass yAxis=upsampled_count() to the events-stats endpoints and execute sum(sample_weight) on datasets/projects that were never allowlisted; the gating in is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects is only applied to the automatic count() rewrite, not to direct user-supplied function calls, so the 'sample_weight exists for all events in allowlisted projects' schema assumption is violated and users get wrong/undefined counts (sample_weight null for unallowlisted projects).

[BUG] _is_error_focused_query uses a raw substring check ('event.type:error' in query) on the lowercased user query, so negated or embedded matches bypass the control. A user query of '-event.type:error' or 'event.type:error_ignored' style strings contains the substring 'event.type:error' and returns True, causing transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling to rewrite count() to upsampled_count() for a query that is explicitly excluding error events; on the discover dataset sample_weight does not exist for transaction rows, so the user gets a 400 from Snuba or silently wrong counts instead of the regular count() the endpoint contract promises.

[ADVISORY] The 60-second eligibility cache has no invalidation wired up, so allowlist changes propagate on a stale-data window. invalidate_upsampling_cache exists but has zero callers in this diff, so an operator removing a project from issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist serves upsampled (inflated) counts for that project for up to 60 more seconds — users see wrong error counts during any allowlist change.

[BUG] `_is_error_focused_query` uses a raw substring check `"event.type:error" in query`, so a negated query like `!event.type:error` (or any string merely containing the token) is classified as error-focused and the sample_weight transform is applied to a query that explicitly excludes errors. A Discover timeseries query with `query=!event.type:error` over allowlisted projects has count() rewritten to sum(sample_weight), inflating counts for non-error events; the test file (test_is_error_focused_query, lines 78-86) only tests the positive, transaction, and empty cases and never exercises negation, so the suite passes while the classifier is wrong.

[ADVISORY] The new upsampling branch inside the `top_events > 0` path (both the `use_rpc` and non-RPC top-events calls switching `y_axes`/`timeseries_columns` to the transformed `final_columns`) has zero test coverage in either new test file. A regression in the topEvents upsampling path (e.g. forgetting the transform, or breaking the `upsampled_count() as count` alias in top-events result mapping) ships undetected; I checked tests/sentry/api/helpers/test_error_upsampling.py and the new OrganizationEventsStatsErrorUpsamplingTest class in tests/snuba/api/endpoints/test_organization_events_stats.py — every request uses plain timeseries (no topEvents parameter), so the top-events transformation code is never executed by any test in this diff.

[ADVISORY] The public entry point `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` and `invalidate_upsampling_cache` are never unit-tested — the new spec file imports only the private helpers and the pure transform, so the 60s cache set/get, the cache-hit short-circuit (`cached_result and _should_apply_sample_weight_transform(...)`), and invalidation are unverified. The integration tests only exercise the cache-miss path, so a bug in the cache-hit branch (e.g. skipping the dataset/request re-check, or a wrong cache-key hash producing cross-project cache poisoning when two project-id tuples hash-collide with different orgs) breaks production behavior with every test still green.

[ADVISORY] `test_error_upsampling_with_transaction_events` stores the transaction event without a subsequent `wait_for_event_count` (unlike the error events in setUp), so the query can run before the event is indexed. The test flakes intermittently in CI depending on event ingestion timing — data[0][1][0]["count"] == 1 intermittently fails as 0, and since the assertion's purpose is to prove the count was NOT upsampled, a flake is indistinguishable from a regression being 'intermittently' caught.

[ADVISORY] `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` wraps its lookups in `try/except Exception: pass` twice, silently swallowing any malformed-structure error and producing an event with no `sample_rate` while the test proceeds. If the error_sampling context shape drifts (e.g. contexts becomes a list after normalization), every upsampling integration test that asserts count == 10 silently degrades to asserting against events with no sample_rate, and the failure appears as a confusing wrong-value in the endpoint test rather than at the factory where the cause lies; the bare except also masks the AttributeError the chained .get is meant to avoid with no distinguishing signal.

[ADVISORY] `test_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` never tests the discover dataset with an empty/absent query, leaving the default-return behavior for the most common Discover query shape (no explicit event.type filter) unverified. Discover queries without an explicit `event.type:error` filter fall through to `return False`, meaning mixed error+transaction timeseries silently lose upsampling; the test table mirrors exactly the three discover cases the implementation handles and omits the case the spec arguably requires (unfiltered Discover queries are error-dominant), so a future change to that fall-through has no test to catch it.

[BUG] transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling replaces count() with sum(sample_weight) under the assumption that 'the database schema ensures sample_weight exists for all events in allowlisted projects', but no migration or backfill in this diff populates sample_weight for events ingested before the sampling feature shipped. For any allowlisted project with historical error events (pre-rollout), sum(sample_weight) returns 0 (or NULL collapsed by toInt64), so the stats endpoint silently reports zero/undercounted errors for those time ranges — silent data loss on read for exactly the orgs that opted into upsampling.

[BUG] The cache key is built with Python's built-in hash(tuple(...)), whose value is randomized per process via PYTHONHASHSEED, so the key computed in invalidate_upsampling_cache (and in any other worker process) differs from the key the writer used. Cache invalidation is a cross-process no-op: when an operator removes a project from the allowlist, invalidate_upsampling_cache deletes a key no process ever wrote, and every web worker keeps serving the stale 'eligible' verdict for up to 60 seconds — queries keep summing sample_weight on a project that just left the rollout. It also collapses the cache to per-process entries, defeating the stated performance optimization.

[ADVISORY] Only the literal column 'count()' is rewritten; every other count-style aggregate (count_unique, user_count, count_if, equations like 'count() / 2', aliased variants) passes through untouched. Dashboard users querying an allowlisted project get upsampled totals from count() but raw (undercounted) values from every sibling aggregation in the same chart, producing internally inconsistent widgets the moment the allowlist is enabled.

[ADVISORY] For the discover dataset, upsampling is gated on the literal substring 'event.type:error' appearing in request.GET['query'], but discover queries with no event.type filter return a mix of error and transaction events. The default (unfiltered) discover query silently uses un-upsampled count() for error rows that are sampled, so users see different error counts depending on whether they added event.type:error to the query — a same-data-different-answer inconsistency during the entire rollout window.

[ADVISORY] The only writer that derives sample data from the error_sampling context is the test factory's _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling, added in this same diff, and it populates a 'sample_rate' key on normalized data rather than any sample_weight field the SnQL function reads. The production ingestion path in this diff contains no code that materializes contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate into the sample_weight column the new upsampled_count() aggregation sums — the feature is a ships-inert read-side transform whose correctness depends entirely on code outside this diff (the sentry-repo submodule), and if that writer is absent or backfills late, every upsampled query returns 0.

[BUG] `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` checks `client_sample_rate` with truthiness (`if client_sample_rate:`), so a valid client_sample_rate of 0.0 is silently treated as absent and `sample_rate` is never set on the event. Any event stored with `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate = 0.0` (client-side sampling fully disabled — a legitimate, even common, configuration) gets no sample_rate, so its sample_weight defaults and upsampled counts computed via `upsampled_count()` are wrong for that event; nothing errors or logs.

[BUG] `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` rewrites `count()` to `upsampled_count() as count` (sum of the `sample_weight` column) while relying on the comment's assumption that sample_weight exists for all events in allowlisted projects — but any event in an allowlisted project that lacks sample_weight makes the Snuba query fail, and the endpoint has no error handling for that, returning a raw 500. The moment a project is added to `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist`, every historical event stored before the sampling context existed (and any event from an SDK not sending the context) has no sample_weight, so every org stats query with yAxis count() against that project 500s — where the same request returned 200 with plain count() before the allowlist flip. The failure mode is unobservable until users see the 500.

[ADVISORY] `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined but has no caller anywhere in this diff, and the eligibility cache is written with a fixed 60s TTL keyed only on (org, project_ids). Operators toggling the allowlist option get up to 60 seconds of stale behavior with no way to force it: a project removed from the allowlist keeps being upsampled (and if removal was to stop the sample_weight 500s above, the outage persists the full TTL); conversely a newly added project takes 60s to start upsampling. The invalidation hook existing but unwired suggests the rollout story was never finished.

[ADVISORY] In the top_events path, only `y_axes`/`timeseries_columns` are transformed; `selected_columns` from `get_field_list`, `equations` from `get_equation_list`, and any count inside an equation or other aggregate referencing count are left as plain count(), so a top-events response mixes upsampled series values with unupsampled selected/equation values in the same payload. Users running topEvents with an equation like `equation|count() * 2` or comparing the series count to a table column count on the same allowlisted project get two different definitions of 'count' in one 200 response, with no indication which is which — a silent partial transformation reported as success.

[ADVISORY] For the discover dataset, `_is_error_focused_query` only returns True when the literal substring `event.type:error` appears in the raw lowercased query string, so discover queries that are error-only by construction (e.g. filtered via `error.handled:false`, issue-tag queries, or where the type filter is applied by other machinery) silently skip upsampling and return unupsampled counts. Users querying the discover dataset for errors without typing the exact `event.type:error` token get counts that are off by the sampling factor with no warning — the API reports success while returning inconsistent magnitude depending on how the query was phrased.
